append.text: **Ps 78:9 *et propítius esto peccátis nostris* → *e sede clemente com os nossos pecados*** (decision `propitius`) — rendered so that it cannot be heard as favouring sin, as asked after 64:4. *Clemência* is mercy shown to a fault: one is clement only with what is a wrong, and it asks what the Latin asks (mildness in judging; DRB 'forgive', MS1932 'perdoa'). *clemens / cleméntia* never occur in the Latin psalter (grep), so it collides with nothing; *perdoar* stays dimíttere's (24:18; the Our Father), *misericordioso* miséricors's (77:38 has both words). **Tested: the ambiguity reader heard 'forgive our sins' first and 'be lenient toward them' second — no reading of favouring**; the Latinist passed it on both drafts; the stylist did not remark. The verse is said alone (Lenten Tract 78:8–9; this psalm's Thursday Matins antiphon *Ádjuva nos … et propítius esto peccátis nostris*; the Nat2-0 versicle), which is why it was ruled here and not left to the row. **Proposed for the family where the object is a sin:** 24:11 *sereis clemente com o meu pecado*, 64:4 *vós sereis clemente com as nossas impiedades*, 77:38, 102:3 *que é clemente com todas as tuas iniquidades*; *propício* stays where the object is a person or land (98:8 *propítius fuísti eis*, the canticle's 32:65 *propítius erit terræ*); 129:4a *propitiátio* decides locally. Cost: the Latin's word is not kept where its object is a sin. Options in Ps 78: *sede propício aos*, *perdoai*, *sede-nos propício apesar dos*, *sede indulgente com*.
**Ps 78:1 *polluérunt templum sanctum tuum* → *macularam o vosso templo santo*** — as 73:7 (the paired psalm); the ambiguity reader listed *macularam* as unknown; kept.

**Ps 78:4 applied: *subsannátio et illúsio* → *zombaria e escárnio*** (43:14's shared words copied, *riso / escárnio* varying as the Latin varies). The ambiguity reader listed *escárnio* unknown; kept.

**Ps 78:4 *Facti sumus oppróbrium vicínis nostris* → *Tornamo-nos uma afronta para os nossos vizinhos*** (43:14's words). **78:12 *impropérium ipsórum, quod exprobravérunt tibi* → *a afronta com que eles vos afrontaram*** — the stylist heard a same-root jingle and asked *insultaram*: refused, the Greek has the figure (ὀνειδισμὸν … ὠνείδισαν), as 68:10; option.
**Ps 78:9 *Ádjuva nos* → *Auxiliai-nos*** (as 43:26); the stylist asked *Ajudai-nos* — refused for the family, option `adjuva`.
**Ps 78:9 *Deus, salutáris noster* → *Deus, nosso Salvador*** — as 64:6; no reader remarked.
**Ps 78:13 *oves páscuæ tuæ* → *as ovelhas da vossa pastagem*** — as 73:1; no reader remarked.
**Ps 78:11 *fílios mortificatórum* → *os filhos dos que foram mortos*** (two syllables shorter than *entregues à morte*, which is the option); no reader remarked.

**Ps 78:11 *pósside* (imperative) → *tomai posse de*** — *possuí* is also 'I possessed' (rule 3) and the object is a noun (D13 does not help); DRB 'take possession of'. The ambiguity reader heard 'seize'; kept.

**Ps 78:12 *redde vicínis nostris séptuplum in sinu eórum* → *pagai sete vezes aos nossos vizinhos no seio deles*** — the lap kept (as 73:11 *seio*); the stylist's order. The ambiguity reader did not know *seio*.
**Ps 78:8 *páuperes facti sumus nimis* → *nos tornamos pobres sem medida*** (as 37:9); *muito pobres* option; no reader remarked.

**Ps 78:10b *gémitus compeditórum* (the same Greek) → *o gemido dos acorrentados*** — not merged: the Latin word is another and names the iron (rule 5); *prisioneiros* option. The ambiguity reader listed *acorrentados* unknown; kept.

terms: | pomórum custódia (78:1 *posuérunt Jerúsalem in pomórum custódiam*) | *como cabana de vigia do pomar* | open | Ps 78:1 (ὀπωροφυλάκιον, the orchard-watcher's hut; the Hebrew's 'ruins' not followed). Draft 1 *cabana de guardar frutos* was heard as a storage shed (ambiguity reader) and found flat (stylist); v2 the stylist's noun. The Latinist asked *reduziram … a* (v1) and *como guarda de frutos* (v2): held, both options — *puseram* keeps the anaphora with 78:2 *Posuérunt*. Isa 1:8's *tugurium in cucumerario* is a kin image (not in the psalter). |

| anticipáre nos (78:8 *cito antícipent nos misericórdiæ tuæ*) | *depressa venham ao nosso encontro as vossas misericórdias* | open | Ps 78:8 (προκαταλαβέτωσαν). Draft 1 *nos antecipem* (as 76:5 *anteciparam*): the stylist called it a Latinism with no clear sense and the ambiguity reader found it odd; v2 the stylist's, passed the Latinist gate. The Lenten Tract sets this verse. *præveníre* elsewhere may want the same phrase (places not yet counted). |

| intróire in conspéctu (78:10b) | *chegar à presença* (*chegue à vossa presença o gemido*) | open | Ps 78:10b only; 118:170 *Intret … in conspéctu tuo → Entre … na vossa presença* stands. Here the subjunctive *entre* followed two prepositional *entre* (78:10) and two readers heard 'between'; *chegue* (MS1932) taken; the v2 Latinist (minor) wants *entre* back — option. |
| morticína (78:2) | *os cadáveres* | open | Ps 78:2 (θνησιμαῖα; properly carrion). *as carcaças* keeps the contempt, option. No reader remarked. |

| desoláre (78:7 *locum ejus desolavérunt*) | *deixar deserto* (*e deixaram deserto o seu lugar*) | open | Ps 78:7 (ἠρήμωσαν); the cognate *desolar* is heard as 'sadden' in Brazil; no reader remarked. |
formulas: | *Dómine, ne memíneris iniquitátum nostrárum antiquárum: cito antícipent nos misericórdiæ tuæ, quia páuperes facti sumus nimis. V. Adjuva nos, Deus, salutáris noster: et propter glóriam nóminis tui, Dómine, libera nos: et propítius esto peccátis nostris, propter nomen tuum* (78:8–9; the Lenten Tract *Dómine, non secúndum*, missa Quadp3-3 and the Lenten ferias — grep) · *Ádjuva nos, * Deus, salutáris noster: et propítius esto peccátis nostris* (the Thursday Matins antiphon, Psalmi matutinum) · *V. Propter glóriam nóminis tui, Dómine, líbera nos. R. Et propítius esto peccátis nostris propter nomen tuum* (Nat2-0) · *Effudérunt sánguinem Sanctórum velut aquam in circúitu Jerúsalem: et non erat qui sepelíret* (78:3; the Innocents, 12-28) | *Senhor, não vos lembreis das nossas iniquidades antigas, depressa venham ao nosso encontro as vossas misericórdias: porque nos tornamos pobres sem medida. Auxiliai-nos, Deus, nosso Salvador: e por causa da glória do vosso nome, Senhor, livrai-nos: e sede clemente com os nossos pecados, por causa do vosso nome* · *Auxiliai-nos, Deus, nosso Salvador: e sede clemente com os nossos pecados* · *…e não havia quem os sepultasse* | open — Ps 78; the propitiári row's ruling lives here |
